title: Low-Density Steels: Complex Metallurgy for Automotive Applications
abstract: Conne´table et al.<sup>26</sup> did not find the thermodynamic model in Ref. 25 satisfactory and reassessed the Fe-Al-C system. They proposed a new CALPHAD description of the j-phase based on their order– disorder model for the face-centered cubic (fcc) phase with four substitutional sublattices but restricted the carbon contents to 20 mol.% C. together with new ab initio calculations, the latter described elsewhere.<sup>27</sup> The fcc and bcc interactions in the Al-C system were revised using experimental results from the ternary system,<sup>11</sup> something that was not done before. In the Al-Fe system, the fcc description (c-loop) was improved with the help of an ordering contribution. These revisions improved the ternary description of the fcc and bcc phases where they used the experimental tie lines given in Ref. 11 at 1200C as a guide. The comparison of the modeling with the experimental isothermal sections was satisfactory and in the case of the isopleths was very good. The rather large solubility of carbon in ferrite shown at 800C and 1000C in Ref. 11 was assumed to have been caused by inaccuracies in the electron probe microanalysis measurements and is not reproduced by the model. The Al-Fe system was further revised by Sundman et al.<sup>28</sup> using a foursublattice model for the bcc phase (in addition to the already modeled fcc phase) and using the most recent experimental data.
